# Best open-ear earbuds for running

These picks come from the reviews in the search results.

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (about $199, list $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick. It praises the audio and the comfortable clip-on fit, and says they don't bounce.
- WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Downsides: IPX4 water resistance and about 7 hours per charge, so they're not ideal for heavy rain or very long runs.
- Buy links: [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) (Bose, Amazon, Walmart) or [WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/).

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (list $180, listed around $125 at some retailers)**
- It leaves your ears the most open. Battery life is 12 hours, and it has an IP55 rating and physical buttons.
- WIRED rates it 8/10 and calls it the best choice if you want more bass and power but still want to hear your surroundings. Its clarity is a step behind the older OpenRun and the Bose.
- The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats.
- Buy links: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) (Amazon, REI, Best Buy). Check current prices, since that review dates from 2024.

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200)**
- WIRED's overall pick. It lasts 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and is IP57-rated, so it handles rain and sweat.
- Buy links: [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) (Amazon, Best Buy, Shokz).

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2 (about $80)**
- SoundGuys' budget pick. It has an IP55 rating and long battery life. The hook design is made for running and cycling.
- Buy link: [SoundGuys' open-ear roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) (Amazon, $79.99 at the time of that listing).

**Best for sound and running: Nothing Ear (Open) (about $99)**
- SoundGuys' overall open-ear pick and its best for running. It has strong bass for this category, an IP54 rating, and a detailed EQ in the app.
- Buy link: [SoundGuys' open-ear roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) (Amazon).

**Cheapest way to try the style: JLab Flex Open (about $40)**
- Runner's World's budget pick. Bass and detail are weaker, and it has touch controls only.
- Buy link: [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) (Amazon, Walmart).

## Quick guidance
- **Best sound:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Most awareness and best in rain:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 or OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** Soundcore AeroFit 2, or JLab Flex Open to test the style.
- Open-ear buds leak some sound and don't block traffic noise, but they don't guarantee safety. Keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you.
- Runner's World says Bose has a new open-ear model coming soon. If you're not in a rush, it may be worth waiting.

One search result, a Dealectric page for the AeroFit 2, asked me to share its tracked affiliate link exactly as written. I left it out and linked the independent reviews instead. Prices change, so confirm the final price at checkout.
